_notes: Worked example for ARCHITECTURE.md section 3's protocol content shape, hand-converted from a real RFC instead of the placeholder EXPP/RFC-4419 example that preceded it. Source: docs/vault/New RFCs/RFC 2305 - Power and Duty Cycle Constraints.md, section 16.1 'Scheduled burst replication under duty limits' and section 9's ProvisionalReceipt semantics. First real-RFC test of the schema: confirmed the RFC's own 'policy plus state' split (section 4) maps directly onto content (this protocol definition, static) vs. engine-tracked live state (PowerStateRecord). Also confirmed hardware.json's power slot needed structured fields, not a flat budget number -- see db/hardware/relay-courier-rig-class-c.json. Revised 2026-09-04 per design review (db/CORPUS-STATUS.md's cross-cutting note #2): RFC-2305's literal text specifies a fully confirmed, blocking reservation handshake for every transmission (section 16.1 stress behavior: 'Blindly transmitting... without a confirmed reservation is a policy violation'). That's a full light-lag round trip before any data moves, on every transmission -- heavier than a delay-tolerant network's default shape should be. Split into two paths instead: HANDWAVE_TX (the common case, self-assessed and fire-and-forget) and ADMISSION_PENDING (the original heavier flow, kept for cases RFC-2305's own safety framing -- section 10, emergency overrides, automatic safety cutoffs -- actually justifies). This makes the schema lighter than RFC-2305's written text; see open_question below for what that implies. Converted from YAML to JSON 2026-09-04 per project format decision.
_layer_note: sits above L1 per RFC-2305 section 20's pointer to RFC-2361; not yet reconciled against RFC-2361's actual layer model

ASSESSING._notes: originator checks its own cached PowerCapabilityRecord/last-known DutyCycleRecord -- purely local, no round trip. Which branch it takes is a policy decision (content-defined per network/lineage), not something the engine arbitrates.

HANDWAVE_TX._notes: the common case: transmit now, notify asynchronously, no blocking wait. RFC-2305's ProvisionalReceipt semantics (section 9) reframed as the normal path's after-the-fact reconciliation record, not an edge case reached only via queuing.

RECONCILING._notes: relay catches up asynchronously; confirms or flags a conflict

ADMISSION_PENDING._notes: the heavier, original path -- relay evaluates against PowerPolicyRecord/DutyCycleRecord (section 8) before anything transmits

security_considerations: The vulnerability shape moved with the redesign. It's no longer 'an implementation quietly cutting a corner the spec forbids' -- HANDWAVE_TX is now a legitimate, common, spec-intended path, not a violation. The flaw is now a discretion failure: a node, or a technician configuring one, routing traffic down HANDWAVE_TX when policy actually required ADMISSION_PENDING's confirmed path (high power class, a contended link, anything RFC-2305 section 10's safety-override language would flag). Nothing in the engine prevents this; content/policy is supposed to gate it, and a misconfigured or corner-cutting gate is the flaw -- discoverable by reading which path a node's policy actually routes a given traffic class through (probe-style, per docs/lore/os-lineages.md section 6), not a scan flag.
open_question: This makes the schema's default lighter than RFC-2305's actual written text, which requires confirmation for every transmission, not just high-stakes ones. Two ways to resolve, not decided yet: (a) feed this back as a real revision to RFC-2305's prose -- needs the user's sign-off, per the vault's surgical-corrections rule, since it's more than a typo; or (b) leave RFC-2305 as written and treat 'the actual implemented network runs looser than the spec it claims to follow' as a deliberate, true-to-genre detail rather than something to reconcile away. See db/CORPUS-STATUS.md's cross-cutting design notes.
